chunks: It will seem as if it has come to you
all of a sudden, silenced those who were whispering to you, separated your group, destroyed your doings, devastated your houses and altered your successors,
distribute your estate among the chief relatives, who did not give you any benefit, or the grieved near ones who could not protect (you), or those rejoicers who did not lament (you).

key_terms.نَجِيَّكُمْ: your whisperers / those speaking in private

ai.seo_question: How does death suddenly change the social and familial status of a person according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali employs vivid rhetorical imagery to depict death as a sudden, disruptive force that silences intimate counsel and fractures social gatherings, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the unpredictability of the hour of demise. The passage underscores the futility of worldly attachments, noting that heirs—whether close kin, grieving relatives, or rejoicing strangers—inevitably partition the estate, illustrating the transient nature of human status and wealth in the face of divine decree.

en.sayed-ali-raza: It will seem as if it has come to you
all of a sudden, silenced those who were whispering to you, separated your group, destroyed your doings, devastated your houses and altered your successors
to distribute your estate among the chief relatives, who did not give you any benefit, or the grieved near ones who could not protect (you), or those rejoicers who did not lament (you).
